Why bold text pastes into fields that have no bold button

Of the styled alphabets tucked into Unicode's Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols block, the serif bold run starting at U+1D400 is the one you can rely on almost anywhere. It is not a font setting and it does not switch your text to a heavier weight: each letter is a separate character that was drawn bold from the start. Bold is also one of the few styles here with its own digits, at U+1D7CE, so a year keeps its weight instead of dropping back to plain figures.

The obvious home for it is a plain-text field that offers no formatting at all: a spreadsheet header row, the first line of a bio, a pinned note. The catch is that these are not the letters anyone types into a search box, so a bold name is a name nobody can look up, and screen readers either mangle the run or pass over it. Keep it to headings and display names rather than body copy.

Where Bold text works, and where it does not

WorksWorks in most bios, posts, display names and chat — X, Instagram, TikTok, Discord, Reddit. Watch outRefused by real-name fields (Facebook, LinkedIn's name field) and unsearchable: these are separate characters from ordinary letters, so nobody will find you by typing your name.

Bold questions

Why do the numbers change as well?

Bold is one of a handful of these alphabets that Unicode gave matching digits, at U+1D7CE. Most of the other styles stop at the fifty-two letters, so a price or a date falls back to ordinary figures in the middle of a styled line. With bold you can set a whole heading, numerals included, without that seam showing.

Will Facebook accept this in my name field?

No. Facebook and LinkedIn validate real-name fields against ordinary letters and reject these characters outright. They do go through in a bio, an about section or a post, but remember that they are separate characters from A to Z, so nobody reaches you by typing your name into a search field.

Is bold text bad for accessibility?

In a paragraph, yes. Screen readers treat mathematical alphanumerics inconsistently, spelling them out, renaming them or skipping them without a word. A bold display name costs a listener one line. A bold sentence costs them the sentence, so leave the plain version in your text and save the styling for a heading.
